title: Restoring an AcmeDB snapshot
intro:
Restoring a snapshot is the half of the AcmeDB 2.0 snapshot story that
nobody rehearses until the night it matters. Taking snapshots is
automatic once the hourly schedule is on; getting one back is a
deliberate act, and it is worth doing calmly and in the same order every
time. A restore never touches the live primary. It lands in a scratch
instance first, where you can check row counts, run the queries that
prompted the restore in the first place, and decide whether the point
you picked is actually before the damage. Only then do you promote the
scratch copy or copy the rows you need back across. The catalog keeps
every snapshot inside the retention window, so the first move is always
to list what exists and how fresh it is, and the second is to pick a
restore point with some margin before the incident started. Teams that
skip the scratch step tend to restore the wrong second and have to do it
twice, under more pressure, with the same people. This page collects the
blocks a restore needs: the order of operations, the checks to tick off
before you start, the one command that opens every restore, and the line
from the docs that says how far back you can go.

sources.quote: Run acmedb snapshot list | head -5 to see the newest snapshots.
Snapshots are online, incremental, and restorable to any point in the last seven days.
